newsitem.title: UK: UK shares open at record high as sterling dips.
newsitem.headline: UK shares open at record high as sterling dips.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index leapt to a record high at the start of trading on Thursday, as growing hopes for no increase in interest rates set the pound lower -- taking the pressure off overseas earners and exporters.
Extending Wednesday's record gains, the FTSE 100 was up 24.1 points at 4,243.2 by 0837 GMT after earlier setting a record 4,244.0 -- surpassing the peak of 4,227.5 set yesterday.

Shares shrugged off a weak close on Wall Street and were led higher by the likes of major oils stocks, which benefit from a strong dollar, and British Steel, recently subject to savage earnings downgrades because of sterling strength.
